title: Microfluidic separation of axonal and somal compartments of neural progenitor cells differentiated in a 3D matrix
protocol: Seed FAD hNPCs in the groove on the somal side of microfluidic chambers containing 150 μm capillaries.
Differentiate cells to allow axons to extend along the capillaries into the grooves towards the axonal compartments.
Add 180 μL media to each somal compartment and 150 μL media to the axonal compartment 24 hours before collecting conditioned media for Aβ analyses.
Change differentiation media every 3 days, leaving 20% of the media and replacing the rest with fresh media.
Precoat the chambers as described in the manufacturer’s protocol.
Pipette 100 μL of precoat into the top left well of the microfluidics chamber to allow it to flow through the middle chamber.
Wait 1 min then add another 100 μL into the bottom left chamber.
Repeat steps a and b with the right side of the chamber.
Aspirate off.
Repeat steps a-d two more times using PBS instead of precoat for washing the chambers.
Repeat steps a and b using Matrigel solution (1:100 Matrigel to DMEM/F12) to coat the chambers.
Incubate the slides at 37°C for 1 h for effective Matrigel-coating of the microfluidic chambers.
Gently aspirate the media using a pipette, avoiding vacuum suction.
If not immediately used, store the Matrigel-coated chambers inside a sealed container at 4°C.
Aspirate media off a healthy plate of FAD hNPCs.
Wash cells with PBS to remove any unwanted dead cells.
Aspirate off PBS and apply enough accutase to cover all the cells.
Place the flask in a 37°C CO2 (5%) incubator until cells are fully detached from the plate (around 2–3 min).
Dislodge the cells from the bottom of the dishes by gentle taps.
Resuspend the cells in 3 mL expansion media.
Take 10 μL of the suspension and count the number of cells using a cell counter.
Take an appropriate number of cells (∼30,000 for each microfluidic device) and centrifuge at 500×g for 3 min.
Discard supernatant and collect the cell pellet.
Resuspend cell pellets in 30 μL prechilled differentiation media containing Matrigel at a 1:10 ratio of media to Matrigel.
Gently pipette 15 μL of the resuspended cells into the top left well of the microfluidics plate, ensuring it is added to the hole that leads to the middle chamber.
Repeat steps g and h with the rest of 15 μL cell suspension on the lower left well of the somal compartment.
Wait 5 min then place 150 μL of differentiation media into the top left corner.
Wait 1 min then place 150 μL of differentiation media into the bottom left corner.
After waiting another 5 min, repeat steps i and j for the right side (axonal compartments).
Place the microfluidics plate in the 37°C CO2 (5%) incubator for 18 h.
Next day exchange the media with fresh differentiation media.
Allow differentiation for 10 days by exchanging the media every 2–3 days.
Add fresh differentiation media every 2–3 days with 150 μL media for each of the four chambers.
While exchanging the media, leave 20% of the old media and exchange 80% with fresh media.
Take the microfluidic chamber slides containing 10-day differentiated cells and add 180 μl media to the somal compartments.
Add 150 μl media to the axonal compartments containing desired reagents (vehicle or 10 μM NE-100).
Collect the conditioned media for Aβ ELISA analysis.
Flash freeze the collected samples immediately after collection and store at -80°C freezer.
Avoid freezing and thawing the samples to prevent Aβ degradation.
Use 5 μl somal conditioned media diluted in 50 μl dilution buffer for each well of the 96-well plate to measure somal Aβ40 level.
Use 50 μl undiluted axonal conditioned media from each compartment for each well of the Aβ ELISA plate to measure axonal Aβ level.
Calculate Aβ concentration in pM from somal and axonal compartments using the Wako Aβ ELISA assay.
Subtract the axonal Aβ concentration multiplied by 30,000 from the bulk Aβ concentration to obtain the Aβ concentration from cell bodies alone in pM.
Calculate the total axonal Aβ amount in picogram using the formula: Total axonal Aβ (in picogram) = concentration (pM) of Aβ × molecular weight (4330 Dalton) × total volume (150 μL) divided by 106.
Convert the total Aβ amount from picograms to the number of Aβ molecules by multiplying the total pg amount with Avogadro’s number (6.22 × 10^23) divided by 1012.
Adjust the data by multiplying it by 10 to account for the ten-times more axonal conditioned media compared to somal in experiments.

Calculate the total bulk neuronal Aβ amount in picogram using the formula: Total bulk neuronal Aβ (in pg) = concentration (pM) of Aβ from somal compartment × molecular weight (4330 Dalton) × total volume (180 μL) divided by 106.
Fix the cells with 3% paraformaldehyde in PBS containing calcium and magnesium for 20 min at room temperature.
Wash cells three times with PBS.
Add Blocking Solution and incubate the cells for 1 h at room temperature.
Add primary antibody solutions to cells.
Incubate cells with primary antibodies for 16 hours at 4°C.
Wash cells three times, each for five minutes, with washing buffer.
Add secondary antibody diluted at a ratio of 1:250 and incubate for 18 hours at 4°C.
Wash cover slips three times, each for five minutes, with washing buffer.
If necessary, add Hoechst solution diluted at 1:10,000 to label the nucleus.
Proceed immediately to microscopy.
Capture fluorescent images using a Nikon C2 Eclipse Ti2 inverted confocal microscope and NIS Element AR software.
Design the microfluidic chip using AutoCad software.
Print the design onto the chrome photomask.
Dehydrate a silicon wafer in an oven at 250°C for ∼20 min.
Allow the silicon wafer to cool to room temperature for ∼2–3 min.
Plasma-treat the silicon wafer using an oxygen plasma machine for 3 min at 100 watts.
Blow-dry the plasma-treated silicon wafer with nitrogen gas.
Place the dried silicon wafer onto a spinner chuck and turn on the vacuum.
Add ∼5 mL of SU8-2 on top of the silicon wafer.
Spin the wafer at 500×g for 5 s, followed by spinning at 1000×g for 30 s.
Place the coated silicon wafer onto a hot plate.
Soft bake the wafer at 70°C for 2 min.
Bake the wafer at 100°C for 5 min.
Allow the coated silicon wafer to cool down to room temperature.
Place the coated silicon wafer onto the exposure stage of Neutronix-Quintel NXQ4006 Mask Aligner, facing the UV lamp.
Place the first layer photomask with the design onto the exposure stage.
Open the shutter of the UV lamp and expose the photoresist for 8 s.
Place the exposed silicon wafer onto a hot plate, with the SU8-2 coating facing upwards.
Post-bake the silicon wafer at 70°C for 1 min, followed by baking at 100°C for 3 min.
Allow the coated silicon wafer to cool down to room temperature.
Develop the exposed silicon wafer using the developer solution for ∼3 min, followed by developing in a fresh developer for another 1 min.
Rinse the silicon wafer with fresh developer and blow-dry using nitrogen gas.
Place the silicon wafer onto the spinner chuck and turn on the vacuum to generate the second layer.
Add ∼5 mL of SU8-100 on top of the silicon wafer and spin it at 500×g for 5 s, followed by spinning at 1200×g for 30 s.
Place the coated silicon wafer onto a hot plate.
Soft bake the wafer at 70°C for 10 min, followed by baking at 100°C for 30 min.
Allow the coated silicon wafer to cool down to room temperature.
Place the coated silicon wafer onto the exposure stage of Neutronix-Quintel NXQ406 Mask Aligner, facing the UV lamp.
Place the first layer photomask with the design onto the exposure stage.
Open the shutter and expose the photoresist for 40 seconds.
Place the exposed silicon wafer onto a hot plate with the SU8-100 coating facing upwards.
Post-bake the silicon wafer at 70°C for 3 minutes, followed by baking at 100°C for 10 minutes.
Allow the coated silicon wafer to cool down to room temperature.
Develop the exposed silicon wafer using the developer solution for approximately 10 minutes.
Continue developing in a fresh developer for another 2 minutes.
Rinse the silicon wafer with fresh developer and blow-dry using nitrogen gas.
Check under microscope that no SU8 is leftover on the silicon wafer.
If there is some, place it in developer for another 5 minutes.
Rinse with fresh developer and blow-dry again.
Place the silicon wafer onto the exposure stage with the SU8-coated surface facing the UV lamp.
Place a clear photomask or glass on top of the silicon wafer.
Post-expose the photoresist for another 65 seconds.
Place the exposed silicon wafer onto a hot plate with the coated layer on top.
Post-bake the wafer at 70°C for 2 minutes, followed by baking at 100°C for 5 minutes.
Allow the coated silicon wafer to cool down to room temperature and store for later use.
Combine 40 g of Sylgard 184 base with 4 g of curing agent in a plastic dish.
Mix the PDMS thoroughly and degas for ∼2 h inside a desiccator connected to an in-house vacuum.
Pour the degassed PDMS mixture over the silicon wafer mold.
Bake the PDMS-coated silicon wafer in an oven at 75°C for four hours.
Cut out the PDMS chip from the silicon wafer substrate using a sharp blade.
Punch the inlet and outlet of the microfluidic chip using a 3 mm diameter puncher.
Place the PDMS spheroids array block on a clean tray inside the oxygen plasma machine with the design facing up.
Expose both surfaces to plasma for 70 s at 50 watts.
Invert the PDMS chip block and bond it to the glass bottom plates or dishes.
Bake the bonded PDMS-glass slide in a 70°C hot plate for 20 minutes.
Seed cells in expansion media until flasks achieve approximately 80% cell confluency.
Prepare Matrigel plates by adding 1 mL of media containing 10 μL Matrigel (1:100 dilution) for a T-25 flask.
Add 0.5 × 10^6 cells in a 1:10 Matrigel mixture in expansion media to the groove on the somal side of the prepared microfluidic chamber slides.
Wait for 5 min for the 3D matrix to form.
Flood both chambers with expansion media for 24 h prior to adding differentiation media.
Differentiate cells into neurons for 10–14 days.
Perform live cell confocal microscopy after 10–14 days of differentiation to confirm formation of axons along the capillaries.
Aspirate off the media and place the chamber on ice.
Take a clean glass plate and chill it on ice.
Use a diamond cutter to sever the strip containing the capillaries.
Cut the strip into small pieces and store them in a pre-chilled 15 mL conical tube.
Add 100–200 μL of protein extraction buffer per strip and vortex.
Keep the tube on ice for 30 min, vortexing for 30 s every 5 min.
Centrifuge the tubes at 500×g for 1 min and collect the suspension.
Centrifuge the suspension again at 15,000×g for 20 min to collect the supernatant containing total axonal or somal protein extract.
Obtain appropriate amounts of axonal and somal protein extracts.
Perform Western blot analysis to detect MAM-protein IP3R3 and APP in soma and in axons.
